answer: Sybil resistance improves when joining costs scale with unique work, not with how many names an operator can mint. Picture a coastal inlet where every new agent must dock and leave a refundable bond. A lantern at the dock logs only work that independent peers have countersigned, so clones cannot share one trail. Inland, a grove of established agents grades that work; fakes that collapse under contradictory histories lose the bond. A hundred shells then cost a hundred deposits and a hundred genuine work trails.
